critical_code_review_comments: server.py _classify_frequency (line 1161) — ranges Mensual 25–35, Bimestral 55–65, Trimestral 85–95, Semestral 175–190, Anual 355–375 with monthly_factor 1/0.5/0.333/0.166/0.083. Reasonable defaults, but 'Quincenal' 13–17 leaves gaps 17–25 (mapped to Irregular) and 'Cada 45 días' 40–50 (with factor ~0.666) is an unusual MX bucket — fine but document if business expects 30-day-strict tolerance.

server.py operations_recurring (line 1183) — cutoff uses today.toordinal() - months_back*30 (approximate 30-day months, not calendar months). Acceptable for a heuristic detector, but mention in docstring (currently only mentions 'últimos 12 meses' in UI).

server.py operations_recurring — provider_name fallback 'Proveedor eliminado' is correct, BUT the system blocks DELETE /providers when transactions reference it (409). So this fallback only triggers for orphan provider_ids (e.g. from imports or manual db edits). Documented in test 'orphan_provider_id_shows_placeholder'.

Operations.jsx — RecurringRow's category column shows the most-used category from the group; works but the value comes from the raw 'category' enum string (e.g. 'services'). Consider mapping to user-friendly labels for consistency with Transactions.jsx.

Dashboard.jsx (line 110) — Promise.all now adds /operations/recurring to the dashboard payload. Endpoint is fast (~5ms for 16 docs) but consider lazy-loading the widget if monthly groups exceed 100 to avoid TTI regressions.
Operations.jsx is 271 lines, single-file component. OK for now but if filters/columns grow, split RecurringRow into its own module.
Non-blocking: server.py still 1899 lines — same comment as iter9/10, recommend splitting into routers (auth, transactions, reimbursements, hub, partners, operations) as future hygiene.
